title: Behavioural finance and client management
objectives: Name common biases and counter them.
Run reviews that keep clients on plan.
body_md:
Clients are human. Good advisers manage **behaviour** as much as portfolios.

| Bias | Effect | Counter |
|---|---|---|
| **Loss aversion** | Selling in a fall | Pre-agree rules; remind of goals |
| **Overconfidence** | Concentrated bets | Show data on average outcomes |
| **Herd behaviour** | Chasing hot themes | Stick to the plan |
| **Recency** | Extrapolating last year | Show long-term ranges |
| **Anchoring** | Fixation on purchase price | Judge on future prospects |
| **Confirmation** | Seeking agreeing views | Present counter-evidence |

## Reviews

- Formal review **yearly** and on life events.
- Report **progress to goals**, not just returns.
- Record changes, rationale and client instructions.

## Communication

Plain language, no jargon, written summary after each meeting, and a calm note in market falls.

> **Exam tip:** Match each bias to its effect.
example: In a 20% fall, a client wants to sell all equity. The adviser reviews the agreed plan, shows the goal horizon and asks if anything in the goals has changed.
say: Your plan was built for falls like this one; let us look at it together.
We measure progress against your goals.
never: Sell everything, the market is going to zero.
Put all your money in what did best last year.
